girl.prompt:
Image 1: family chibi sticker sheet. Use it for the art style (thick black outlines, flat bright colours, chibi proportions, big eyes) and for exactly how the girl looks: copy her face, hair, colouring and clothes from it. Do not copy its scenes, poses, hearts or sticker borders.

Draw the girl four times as separate full-figure chibi characters for a seek-and-find book, arranged in a 2 x 2 grid on a plain pure white background, with wide white space between them so nothing touches. All four are the same size and the same character: wavy shoulder-length brown hair with a fringe, big eyes, rosy cheeks, lavender T-shirt, navy shorts, pink shoes.

1. Top left: standing facing the viewer, smiling, arms relaxed at her sides.
2. Top right: sitting on the ground facing the viewer, legs out in front, hands on her knees.
3. Bottom left: walking towards the right of the picture, seen from the side, mid-step, one arm swinging forward.
4. Bottom right: peeking: only her head, shoulders and two hands are shown, as if she is looking over a low wall, with the drawing ending in a straight horizontal line at chest height and nothing drawn below that line.

01.title: The toy shop
01.prompt:
Image 1: family chibi sticker sheet. Use it for the art style only: thick black outlines, flat bright colours with no shading, chibi proportions with big heads and big eyes, rosy cheeks. Do not copy its people, scenes, poses or sticker borders.

Paint one extremely busy seek-and-find scene for a children's picture book: a huge toy shop on the busiest day of its big sale, packed wall to wall like a crowded market, seen from high above so the whole floor is visible.

The crowd comes first: at least 150 small cartoon people in the same chibi style fill the floor of the shop, each no taller than one-twentieth of the picture's height (a little bigger at the front, a little smaller at the back). Every face is different: children and grown-ups of every age, many different skin tones, face shapes and hairstyles (curly, straight, short, long, plaits, ponytails, bald, grey), some in hats, caps or headbands, a few in glasses, clothes in reds, yellows, oranges, greens, teals, blues and pinks with stripes, spots and patterns. They are doing lots of different things: queuing at three tills, pushing prams and trolleys, carrying stacks of boxes, children riding ride-on toys, playing with the train set, trying on costumes and crowns, hugging teddies, crying over a dropped ice cream, a dad asleep on a bench, staff on ladders stocking shelves, a child hiding in a pile of plush toys, a birthday party group in party hats.

The toys fill the shelves around the edges and a few islands in the middle: a mountain of teddy bears and plush animals, dolls and dolls' houses, a toy train on a big track, a bin of bouncy balls spilling across the floor, building block towers, toy cars and a race track, dinosaurs, rocking horses, a puppet theatre, a rack of dress-up costumes, kites and balloons hanging from the ceiling.

Leave small patches of open floor between the groups of people, spread across the whole picture. Keep the ceiling to a thin band at the top. Nobody wears lavender, light purple, navy, cream or dark green, nobody has a full beard, and nobody has their hair in a high bun.

Every person has exactly two arms and two legs, natural-length arms, and hands with the right number of fingers. No text, letters or numbers anywhere, including on signs, boxes, price tags and shelves. 3:2 landscape, highest resolution.
